subtype: Approach: decides the smallest useful version and defers extras [Thinking]
passage:
Mentor note, Friday demo prep. The campus notes team came in with a list of nine features. Indu wrote them on the board and asked the others one question: "With only two weeks, what does a student need on day one to bring a friend back?" Answers came out loud. "Somewhere to upload notes." "A way to find them." Someone asked about ratings, and Indu said, "Nice, but nobody rates what they cannot find yet." Profiles went the same way. The board ended with two lines under Launch and seven under Later, and the team spent the rest of the hour dividing upload and search between them. I said nothing during the reasoning and only asked when they would show it to a first-year student. They said Tuesday.

Tanuja, project mentor

qa.q: How many lines ended up under Launch and under Later?
qa.a: The board ended with two lines under Launch and seven under Later.

qa.q: How might Indu have felt about the nine-feature list?
qa.a: Indu seemed determined to cut the list down, wanting the team to focus on what a student needs on day one.

qa.q: What could the team do if first-year students ask for ratings?
qa.a: The team could move ratings up the Later list once real requests show that it matters.

qa.q: How might a first-year student see a site with only upload and search?
qa.a: A first-year student might find it simple and useful straight away, since finding notes is the main need.

grounding: Shows a student team choosing the smallest useful launch, upload and search, and postponing other features.
